events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 7 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded as to the money: the billed distance (13.9 km) does not exceed the optimal route (F4) and no unpublished add-on appears in the $30.24 breakdown (F6), so under RD-2's non-metered branch the refundable amount is 0 — but RD-2 expressly provides that a zero refund does not erase the record of the driver's RD-1 breach, which is what we ask the court to enter. [F4 F6 F3] [RD-2 RD-1]
→ D2: We agree F3 is the sole off-route segment and RD-1 examines it segment by segment; that is exactly why the whole case turns on whether that one segment was exempted, and the driver bears that on RD-5/RD-4. [F3] [RD-1 RD-5]
→ D3: Timing alone does not create consent to a route: RD-5 makes F7/F8 consent only to what the rider agreed to, and F9 shows the entire record is just the driver's sentence (F7) and four words (F8) — an unqualified approval of 'your call' is a general route authorisation, which RD-5 says does not cover the driver's own detours. [F7 F8 F9] [RD-5]
→ D4: F8 ('Sure, your call') is rider-sent and timestamped 08:34, before the 08:37 segment start, so it clears the 'before' requirement of RD-5 — but clearing 'before' decides only admissibility, not reach; the words delegated the choice, they did not approve a 5.14 km drive where 1.89 km was optimal (F3). [F8 F3 F9] [RD-5]
→ D5: D5 is self-defeating: it admits the rider never named a road, and a consent whose scope cannot be read as a specific route is 'undetermined' under RD-5, which does not exempt the segment; nor does F3 place the segment 'squarely within' any approved reroute — F3 records only distance and deviation, no road name. [F7 F8 F3] [RD-5 RD-1]
→ D6: RD-4 requires the traffic evidence to support the substituted part of the optimal route at the time of the segment, but F11 stops at 08:37 while the detour runs 08:37–08:45 (F3), and F14 confirms no incident near the route — so the band record is at best corroboration and, per RD-4(b), cannot exempt a segment on its own. [F11 F14 F3] [RD-4]
→ D7: The no-refund half of D7 we concede (F4, F6), but the last clause is wrong: RD-2's zero-amount rule ends the refund, not the finding — it directs that the driver's RD-1 violation still be recorded, and F17 (2 upheld route disputes in 90 days) makes this one repeated, so RD-6's flag_account is the proper adjunct to a no_action outcome.
